Aquality Farms was created to provide affordable access to fresh, nutritious products for our local communities using sustainable agricultural practices. The combination of vertical hydroponic systems and a developing recaptured CO2 plan puts an emphasis on minimizing growing area, energy and water consumption while maximizing yield per square foot. Without the use of pesticides, herbicides, or any other harmful chemicals our natural products are grown all year long in a converted warehouse. Only using 2,000 square feet we are able to grow nearly 24,000 heads of lettuce over a 6 week cycle. In a space half that size we are able to cultivate up to 300 pounds of Lion’s Mane, Oyster, Chestnut, and Reishi mushrooms a week. The nutritional benefits from our lettuce, mushrooms, and various microgreens remain longer due to our local model and commitment to wellness which prioritizes the individual, the community, and the environment. We believe in helping people create a Sustainably Healthy lifestyle. Not all produce is created equal, it has become a matter of convenience and the standard that we view most produce as being healthy when many times it’s the complete opposite. Lettuce sprayed with poison, transported across the country then sold to you at an unfair price is not healthy for yourself, your family, or the environment. Aquality Farms wants to show the next generation that fresh, sustainably healthy food sources are the standard not the exception. Alabama is home to fertile soil, clean water, creative minds, and hard workers that are able to produce the best products using the best practices so keep fresh, keep sustainably healthy, keep Alabama! Read more about Aquality Farms here.

Since then, my family and I have worked to carefully restore the farmhouse while maintaining its original character and charm. Today, Ashley Farm is once again a thriving operation. By leasing surrounding land, I’ve expanded into a growing cattle operation, allowing us to offer high-quality Ashley Farm Beef to your family. Established in 1914, Bartl Farms is a fourth-generation family farm located in Central Baldwin County, Alabama. We consider raising quality cattle to produce quality beef for your family a high privilege that we do not take for granted. The beef you purchase from us is from cattle who are raised on our farm. They are grass-fed and grain finished. Their feed is made on our farm with only the best ingredients grown on our farm. Their food never consists of hormones or antibiotics. We take pride in growing a quality product just as you take pride in providing quality meals for your family. Because we know that it is important to you to know where your food comes from, we consider it one of our most important responsibilities to make sure you are provided with the best beef raised on Bartl Farms. | | Nestled between the busy cities of Pensacola and Mobile, is Gateswood, Alabama. Forested areas mixed with plains rise up in our community where agriculture is a mainstay. A variety of products are found growing here in our natural coastal plains and sandy clay loam soils. Our farm in Gateswood was bought by Anthony Bartl and Tim Bartl in 1977. The property was wooded with some pieces of homesteads left behind from previous use. After a year, the land was converted to crop land. As the farm grew, barns were built for machinery and grain bins were added for the crops. | | We owe our way of life in large part to the generations that came before us. Our family is fortunate enough to have German roots that date all the way back to those who ventured to the United States in the early 1900s. Today's crew share the same passion with modern challenges. | | Our cattle are offered a well balanced diet. When they are weaned from their momma, they are allowed to graze the pasture grass. To meet their ever-changing dietary needs, we also give them homegrown hay. In their last 90-120 days, we will feed them a grain mixture grown fresh on our farm. They are never fed hormones or antibiotics. Our cattle are offered room to move. They are kept in open fields where they have ample room to move and roam. | We use best practices for our crops. We focus on preserving our ground to allow for the best land and soil management available for our crops and cattle. Majority of our fertilizer is chicken litter. | Technology touches just about every aspect of our farm. GPS helps guide our tractors. We utilize GPS with a computer system allowing us to map out each field while pulling soil samples. Soil samples are used to test our soil to enable us to pinpoint what nutrients are in the soil. This allows us to add extra fertilizer only where it is needed. | Relationships are the foundation of our business. We don't always know the answer, but we are fortunate to maintain a network of experts. From butchers to agronomists, bankers, and veterinarians; their wealth of knowledge is impressive, and we like to keep our communication open to these partners. | | When we decided to start the Farm Store at Bartl Farms, we wanted to leverage our experience of cattle feeding and combine it with today's demands of sustainability and traceability. Our customers will always receive beef from cattle locally raised on our farm, beef with no added hormones, aged to perfection, and antibiotic free homegrown feed. Just as you care about what you consume, we want our cattle to have fresh and wholesome feed ingredients. Our cattle feast on our homegrown forages and grains for nutrition each day. We know the cattle, we know the feed, we know the process. That is why we can say that there is no mystery in their history. | | You can typically find us at the Farm Store on Monday and Friday from 2:00pm - 6:00pm and Saturday from 10:00am - 2:00pm. We are almost always available for appointment pick up outside normal business hours, please visit our website to schedule an appointment at bartlfarms.com

The mill was designed and built to service Black Creek Quail Farm. As the mill was brought online it was quickly realized that the mill had plenty of extra capacity that was especially suited for running small, specialized batches of feed which lends itself very well for research. Black Creek Milling grows corn locally and is gathered, dried, tested and then stored. This helps us to be toxic free and consistent with moisture. The mill has a one-ton Scott twin shaft horizontal batch mixer. The mixer is fed by a major scale, 4 minor scales fed by 8 minor bins, 2 micro scales fed by 24 micro bins and computer aided hand adds. The major scale is accurate to 1 pound, the minor scales are accurate to .1 pounds, and the micros are accurate to .02 pounds. Two hand add scales are used in the computer aided hand adds. One is accurate to .01 pounds and the second to .001 pounds. We have one liquid tank of soybean oil, but have a tote hook up to meter other liquids to the mixer as needed. We have pelleting capability with a 60 HP CPM pellet mill and CPM counter flow cooler. We can do pelleting runs as small as 1000 pounds and up to two tons per hour with the cooler being the limiting factor. The mill is also equipped with a CPM crumbler. Hello, our names are Dylan and Kali Gilbert and we are the owners and operators of our farm, Blue Ridge Cattle Co. We are a small, veteran owned first generation farm located in Cullman, AL. We offer bulk Freezer Beef and bulk Pork for purchase. Periodically, we offer beef for purchase in smaller box quantities. Check out our website for the most up to date offerings! We are starting out on this journey after our time in the military has ended but hope to grow to become a respected business in the community providing you with quality beef, pork and livestock. Dylan graduated from the University of Nebraska-Lincoln with a degree in Animal Science, Livestock Production and Management with a minor in Grazing Livestock Systems. While in the Midwest, Dylan gained experience in feedlot settings, giving him valuable insight into what it takes to produce quality livestock resulting in a quality protein product for consumers. At Blue Ridge Cattle Company, we focus on the science behind the efficient growth of livestock by selecting feeding programs that fit the needs of livestock and customers. By doing so, we can ensure that the livestock produce a quality product for the consumer when finished and processed. We believe that quality protein is an essential part of family gatherings, important life events and more - and we want Blue Ridge Cattle Company to be a part of those special moments. Our time in the military gave us many experiences that helped push us toward our lives in agriculture. Not only for the aspect of "being our own boss" but the new-found appreciation for our country, its people and the land. We are passionate about providing for and serving those around us, even outside our military service. Farming is our way to continue to give back to our community in a positive and impactful way. That is also why education, outreach, and advocacy are incredibly important things in the work we strive to do. We would love to connect with other veterans, organizations that serve veterans and more. Please reach out to us if you have an opportunity for us to fit into your organization or if you are someone who has questions about farming, veterans getting into agriculture and more! notes: Hello, we're the Morrison's and we run Earnest Roots Farm. We started getting serious about this way of life in 2017, when our first baby was born. We had tons of questions like "Where does our food come from? Who produces our food? How is our food produced? Why are chemicals used to make it grow? What impact does it have on our health? What impact does it have on our environment? How are the animals raised? What are the animals fed? What are GMO's? What does all those food labels mean?" These are questions that most of the population cannot answer. We have decided to be part of a movement that connects the farmer back to the consumer. "Know your Farmers, Know your Food." - this simple phrase has never been more achievable. Earnest Roots Farm would like to be your farmer and invite you to join us on this journey and bring light to some of these questions and many more. We invite you to come to our farm for milking classes from our family milk cow as well. We strive to produce the healthiest, most nutrient dense and flavorful food we can with quality in mind - not quantity. The meats we offer are free of any additive chemicals or pharmaceuticals, all while being environmentally conscious and positively affecting the ecosystem around us. Using sustainable and regenerative agriculture practices, along with holistic animal management, we work with nature by managing the animals to improve the land. Instead of synthetic, petroleum based, chemical fertilizers we use compost and animal manure with a focus on building soil structure as well as fertility. This is done with movement - animals were not created to be raised on concrete floors in confined houses or feed lots of dirt. God created every plant plant and animal with their own unique characteristics and they thrive in bio diverse environment. Our animals are raised in portable housing and electric netting. This allows us to consistently move them to fresh grass and pasture. All of this working together completely changes the quality of the product; thus, the eating experience is completely different than that of its counterpart. We sincerely thank you for your support. Every time you choose to shop local, you encourage that farmer to do what they do and you provide them with the assets they need continue to grow and provide more and more varieties. Head on over to our online store and take a gander at what we have to offer.

notes: Welcome to Hawkins Homestead Farm. We are a small family owned and operated urban farm that specializes in fresh eggs, organic poultry, value added products, and organic seasonal produce. We had no idea that our search to feed own family in a healthy and sustainable manner would turn into helping feed others, but we’re sure glad it did! | | Our belief is that it is so important that we know what we’re feeding ourselves and where our food comes from. This also holds true in what we choose to put on our bodies, so we also make a line of bath and body products. | | As proud members and certified by The National Poultry Improvement Plan (NPIP), we are committed to the care, health, and safety of our animals and the food we grow. We never use antibiotics or pesticides on anything we have here. Our produce is grown from Non-GMO organic seed, along with Non-GMO organic started plants, and heirloom varieties. It is always fresh and chemical free. | | We have a variety of heritage breed layers who spend their time free ranging. They love to find whatever goodness they can get their hands on and we let them. They’re out early in the day and locked up once they go in at night. We give them the best quality Non-GMO feed that we can find. This ensures they are getting the nutrients needed to continue laying. | | Our meat birds are housed in a brooder while young. Once feathered out, we move them to fresh air and sunshine. This is where they spend the rest of their days. The birds are given the best diet consisting of a Non-GMO organic feed which is rationed each day in addition to what they can find on their own. | | We also grow specifically for our chickens so all our birds receive treats in the form of organic herbs, fruits, and vegetables from our garden with some occasional black oiled sunflower seeds, which they love. | | We try to find a use for almost everything here, so we compost our scraps and our chicken manure. Doing things this way has enabled us to re-purpose and grow some wonderful organics in the garden. | | As an urban farm we live in a community. So while we love and appreciate our customers, we have to protect the bio security of our precious birds and respect the privacy of our neighbors. As a result, we are unable to host visitors at this time. Most business is done through our online site. You may also call, email, or contact us through social media for questions. | | We grow all year long and here for the community. We take pride in what we do and are happy to say that what started out as food for our family has blossomed into food for yours.

Little Creek Farm began with a dream of Patty and Harold Talbot retiring to a cattle farm. Patty was especially keen on cattle as she had grown up on a ranch. Tragically, just as the farm in Tennessee was ready and being stocked, Patty became ill and then passed on. Harold and son Jeff decided to carry on Patty's vision but to move their operation to Florence Alabama so Jeff could be more involved in day to day operations. One day, while riding around to different farms with cattle for sale, the two came across a beautiful set of red cattle near Lawrenceberg Tennessee. They were so taken with the cows, they ended up purchasing the entire Mitchell Daniel herd and moving them to Florence. | Choosing Red Poll cattle has been a tremendous advantage in beginning a new farm. The cattle are extremely easy to handle and the beef is so tender and good it really just sells itself. Another advantage to Red Poll is that they are very efficient and produce at a high stocking rate. | Fortunately, Red Poll cattle do well in managed grazing type operations. With 51 acres and 40 cows, pasture management is crucial to success on our farm. The farm is divided into eight paddocks which can further be subdivided temporarily. Fenceline tanks provide water to each paddock. Such an arrangeemnt allows pastures to regrow while cattle are consuming grass in other cells. In addition to pasture grasses, cattle receive about 5 pounds of natural feed every three days. Beeves being fattened for processing receive about 10 pounds each of natural feed daily, in addition to pasture grasses, during the finishing phase. Such an intensive style of management has caught the attention of many because it has been a unique way to get the most out of the farm's resouces and keep pastures thick and healthy. | Our cattle is sold in several different ways. notes: Scofield Family Farm, where old roots run deep and new memories are always being made. | | The farm was first built in the 1970s by Amanda’s grandparents, who poured their hearts into the homestead and the land around it. They bought the farm and set out to carry on the legacy—breathing new life into the old homestead while keeping the spirit of family and hard work alive. | | The farm also carries another very special piece of family history. Amanda lost her dad, Gary, in 2006. Before he passed, he always dreamed of having a little roadside farm stand called “Preserving Time.” It was his vision of a place where homemade goods, fresh flavors, and simple country living could be shared with others. Years later, with a lot of love and the help of Marcus, that dream became a reality. Today, the roadside stand stands proudly at Scofield Family Farm—helping Amanda keep her daddy’s dream alive and truly preserving a piece of family history. | | Life on the farm looks a little different these days. Amanda spends her weekdays behind the chair as a hair stylist and running her salon boutique in Florala, while Marcus works long days in the oilfield. But when the work boots come off and the weekends roll around, you’ll usually find them back on the farm—tending the land, trying new recipes in the kitchen, and stocking the farm stand with homemade goodness. | | Of course, no farm would be complete without its four-legged crew. Around here you’ll likely be greeted by Poncho, the loyal blue heeler who thinks he runs the place; Tank, the miniature long-haired dachshund with a big personality in a small body; Sassy Montana, the cat who lives up to her name; and Clarice, the most spoiled Nigerian dwarf goat you’ll ever meet. | | Scofield Family Farm is more than just a place on the map. notes: We moved from Moody, AL to Ashland in the spring of 2020 with the dreams of starting a small homestead that would sustain the 2 of us.We waited until our 2 daughters moved out before we started looking for property in the country. When we found our 30 acres we knew instantly it was going to be ours! We knew we would have a few chickens for eggs and meat and a couple of dairy goats for milk since we make soap. Keep in mind, we both grew up in the city and knew nothing about livestock, farming, preserving food and pretty much anything homesteading! In December of 2020, we found a newborn calf in the ditch on our road. We knocked on doors to see if anybody was missing a calf but they all said no. We brought her to our farm and figured out how to care for her. Bottle feedings twice a day at 3:00 a.m. and 3:00 p.m. That had to be the feeding schedule because we both still worked full time. We did that for 13 weeks and after miraculously surviving, we built a bigger area for her to live in and got her a goat as a companion. She now lives at another farm where she can be a cow with other cows! After we got 1 goat we quickly added more goats to our farm and then started breeding goats so we could have their milk. We are up to 16 Nigerian Dwarf goats and are getting lots of milk every day. In the middle of all this we have a big veggie garden that we tend to every day in the summer and have added honey bees! | What do we do on our farm you ask? We make goat milk soap, shave soap, body butter, lip balm and beard oil. We are learning how to make cheese with our goat's milk as well. In our garden we have all kinds of peppers from sweet and mild to face melting super hots! We also have tomatoes, okra, squash, zucchini, beans, peas, corn, melons and luffah. We make our own salsa, hot sauce, spicy salt, pickles, and jams that we sell at the farmer's market. We have fresh, free range chicken eggs that we sell at market as well. We also have t-shirts, sweatshirts, hats and koozies with our logo that we sell at craft shows along with all of our skin products. We have a website in the works that will keep everyone informed on upcoming events and what we have available for sale. | If anybody told us we would be living in a small town growing our our food one day, we both would have laughed in their face! The only regret we have is that we waited until our 40s to do this! What a blessing it is that we get to be stewards of our beautiful land and animals and in return they can take care of us in such a bountiful way that we are able to give to others! Everyday we learn something new and love to share that knowledge with others with the same crazy dream we had.
